clusters.name: Walter moving the family across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours in the trees, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, and Walter and June's rows over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, marking the family's settling into the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, within the year: Walter's heavy drinking, conflict between Walter and Glen over blame for the loan, Glen and Marian's overfunctioning as Glen took over the family's money and the bank talks, Carl's asthma attacks that winter, Nora's bed-wetting in April 1969, and Ida's heart trouble found that May. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, marking the family's settling.

clusters.name: Glen losing his job at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975, within the year: Glen sat in the truck for hours that spring, Glen and Marian fought loudly over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices, Nora stopped eating and lost weight that summer, Nora kept to her room and distanced from her mother, Walter began drinking again after six years off it in December, and by June 1976 Nora was eating again and made the track team, marking the family's settling.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into the house in January 1990, within the year: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and distanced from the rows, Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, and Nora and Hollis rowed most nights by November. Nora's mother drove over twice a week to take her side, and in June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town; by August the eczema cleared, marking the family's settling.
